chapters.n: The first statement names the Godhead: the Father, His Son Jesus Christ, and the Holy Ghost. Latter-day Saints believe these are three distinct beings, perfectly united in purpose.
Each person is accountable for his or her own sins, not for Adam’s. This rejects the idea that we inherit guilt from the Fall; little children, for example, are innocent.
Because of Christ’s Atonement, salvation is open to every person. We accept that gift by obeying the gospel’s laws and receiving its ordinances.

f.g: Christ’s suffering, death, and resurrection that reconcile us to God (literally “at-one-ment”).

chapters.n: The first principles and ordinances: faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, baptism by immersion to wash away sins, and the gift of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of hands. Together they are the doorway into Christ’s Church and the covenant path.

f.w: Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ
Laying on of hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost

chapters.n: To preach and perform ordinances, a person must be called by God through inspiration and ordained by those who hold authority. Priesthood authority is not self-appointed.
Christ’s restored Church follows the pattern of the New Testament Church, with apostles, prophets, and other officers. “Primitive” here means original or earliest.

f.g: the original Church organized by Christ and His Apostles.
Joseph Smith taught that an evangelist is a patriarch.

chapters.n: Spiritual gifts — tongues, prophecy, revelation, visions, healing, and more — are still active today. God did not stop giving gifts after New Testament times.
The Bible is God’s word, though errors entered through transmission and translation. The Book of Mormon is also God’s word and stands as a second witness of Jesus Christ.

f.w: as far as it is translated correctly
the Book of Mormon to be the word of God

chapters.n: Revelation is ongoing: we accept everything God has revealed, everything He reveals now, and expect that He will reveal many more great things. The heavens are not closed.

Latter-day Saints believe in the literal gathering of Israel, the return of the Ten Tribes, a New Jerusalem built in America, Christ’s personal reign on earth, and the earth’s renewal to a paradise-like state.

f.g: the glory of paradise, like Eden before the Fall; see D&C 29:22-25.

chapters.n: A strong statement of religious freedom: we claim the right to worship according to conscience and grant everyone the same right — however, wherever, and whatever they worship.

f.w: according to the dictates of our own conscience

chapters.n: Church members are to obey, honor, and sustain the laws of the lands where they live and respect those who govern.

f.w: subject to kings, presidents, rulers, and magistrates

f.g: local officials who administer the law.

chapters.n: The final article describes the Christian character: honest, true, chaste, kind, virtuous, doing good to all. It echoes Paul (1 Corinthians 13 and Philippians 4) and invites us to seek out everything good wherever it is found.

f.g: kind and generous, wanting good for others.
